rules.name: Employee Access Log Analysis

direction.title: Comprehensive Employee Access Log Review
direction.description: Pull access logs, duty rosters, attendance records, shift changes, and administrator/override events. Look for employees with access to compromised areas, recent disciplinary actions, financial distress indicators, or abrupt behaviour changes.
direction.trigger: Security or access controls were disabled/bypassed in a way that suggests legitimate credentials or internal knowledge of the schedule/layout.
search_targets: Employees present within the incident window
cross_match: Access timestamps against the incident timeline
Present-on-shift list against known associates of other hypotheses
direction.expected_outcome: Confirms whether the security shutdown required legitimate/internal credentials — directly moves the Inside Job hypothesis up or down.

rules.why_template: Inside job hypothesis exceeds 60% — employee access patterns and recent personnel changes are the highest-yield investigation vectors for insider threats.

rules.name: Former Employee Investigation

direction.title: Former Employee Background & Contact Trace
direction.description: Build a list of employees who resigned, were terminated, or were suspended in the last 2 years — especially anyone with knowledge of layout, schedules, or security procedures — and cross-match against current mobile, financial, and location data.
direction.trigger: Inside job hypothesis is active and the method shows familiarity with layout/procedures beyond what a current employee alone would need to demonstrate (i.e. someone who knew it, but isn't there day to day).
cross_match: Former-employee list against current financial distress indicators
Former-employee list against current location near the scene
Former-employee list against other hypotheses' associate names
direction.expected_outcome: Surfaces a short list of ex-staff with both motive/knowledge and current traceability — a fast path to a named suspect.

rules.why_template: Inside job hypothesis is active — former employees combine the layout/procedure knowledge of an insider with the motive profile of a grievance, and are often easier to trace than current staff.
